svMultiPhysics_result.note: This is transient (t=0.005s), not steady-state. The pressure is still developing.

comparison.root_cause: The 1D model uses steady-state assumptions with full flow (5 L/min). The svMultiPhysics run is at t=0.005s (first time step) where flow is still ramping up from zero. The pressure drop at t=0.005s is much lower than steady-state because the flow hasn't fully developed yet.
comparison.what_this_means: The comparison is NOT apples-to-apples. svMultiPhysics ran 2 time steps of a transient simulation starting from zero flow. Our 1D model assumed steady-state at full flow. To properly compare, we need to either: (a) run svMultiPhysics to steady-state (many more time steps), or (b) compare our 1D model at t=0.005s.
comparison.honest_assessment: The svMultiPhysics execution WORKS (solver converged, produced physically reasonable pressure values). But the comparison requires matching time points. This is a methodology issue, not a physics issue.
